```text
                                27:40
  take a closer look at
  how raising impacts
  equilibrium decisions.
  The fundamental question we answer in this lesson is:
  "How will my opponent's betting strategy change with the
  addition of raising?"

  In this lesson we'll find that the equilibrium solutions for
  raising lines look much different than they do for the non-
  raising lines. Raising requires an additional set of logical
  problems to think through and causes both players to
  make more conservative betting decisions. The takeaways
  in this video speak to definitive poker problems, and you
  should begin to understand with more depth how much
  your opponent’s tendencies impact how you should play.

  The A-to-5 game with raises demonstrates how to think
  about river bluff-raising and thin value betting. How do
  you know when thin value betting makes sense? How do
  you know when to bluff-raise the river? These questions
  and more will be elucidated.
```

## PDF page 39

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/GTO%20Crash%20Course%20Strategy%20Guide%20-%20Red%20Chip%20Poker.pdf#page=39)

```text
39 ♠ GTO CRASH COURSE - STRATEGY GUIDE


  3. OOP will raise with an Ace if he checks and IP bets.
  What hand(s) does he check-raise as a bluff? Why?



         OOP check-raise bluffs with Tens to Sevens.
         This is very different from the A-to-5 game
         without raises in which only Fives and Sixes
         bluff. With raises, Tens down to Sevens are
         facing a polarized range, meaning they are
         ahead of all of IP’s bluffs, but behind all of
         her value bets. The reason why Sixes and
         Fives make bad check-raise bluffs in this
                         SHOW ANSWER
         situation is that OOP wants IP to be holding
         a Six or a Five, but when OOP holds a Six
         or a Five he blocks IP from holding those
         hands. Note that all bluff-raising candidates
         are indifferent between raising, calling, and
         folding, which is why they can be used as
         bluffs.
```

```text
40 ♠ GTO CRASH COURSE - STRATEGY GUIDE


  4. Facing a bet, what is the worst hand that IP raises for
  value and as a bluff?



         IP can raise a King for value, since OOP
         must bet some combos worse than a King
         for value. OOP will raise Jacks through
         Sevens as a bluff, because OOP never
         bet Jacks for value,
                         SHOWIPANSWER
                                 treats Jacks as a
         bluffing candidate. Note that all bluff-raising
         candidates are indifferent between raising,
         calling, and folding, which is why they can
         be used as bluffs.
```
